question.text: `Bal Vikas Samiti`, an NPO listed on BSE-SSE via a INR 1.5 crore ZCZP issue, receives an inbound INR 80 lakh foreign CSR contribution from a Netherlands-based donor. Ms. Sunita Patil (SIA) is preparing her Annual Impact Report. Which COMBINATION of regulations governs this foreign contribution and its onward reporting into the AIR?

answer.text: FCRA 2010 (registration and use of a designated bank account for foreign contributions) + SEBI LODR Reg 91E for the AIR and Reg 91F for fund-utilisation reporting + Income Tax Section 11 / 12AB (application of income)
Only FCRA 2010 — because the donor is foreign, SEBI does not apply
Only SEBI (ICDR) Chapter X-A — because the entity is listed on SSE, FCRA stands overridden
Only FEMA 1999 — because any foreign inflow to a Section 8 / NPO is treated as FDI

explanation.text: The Logic: A foreign contribution to a listed NPO triggers a multi-statute cascade. FCRA 2010 governs the foreign contribution itself, including registration and the use of a designated bank account. SEBI LODR Reg 91E governs the Annual Impact Report and Reg 91F governs fund-utilisation reporting for SSE-listed entities. Income-tax Section 11 and Section 12AB govern application of income and registration of the NPO. No single statute overrides the others; compliance is cumulative. The Trap: Saying only FCRA applies ignores the SSE-listed entity's LODR and tax obligations. Treating SSE registration as overriding FCRA is wrong. Treating the foreign donation as FDI under FEMA mischaracterises a charitable grant as an equity inflow. Note: Specific bank-account naming conventions or any references to other regulators' rule numbers should be verified against the current FCRA/SEBI texts before being cited in the AIR.
